perils.severity_note: Hurricane dominates expected building loss: NRI building EAL $254.4M/yr for Palm Beach County (58% of the county's $440.9M total building EAL), rating 'Very High' (score 99.9). Hurricanes within 50 nm since 1950 (HURDAT2 max wind inside radius / closest approach): Cleo 1964 (80 kt/26 nm), Isbell 1964 (80/35), David 1979 (85/30), Irene 1999 (65/19), Frances 2004 (95/30), Jeanne 2004 (105/30), Katrina 2005 (70/39), Nicole 2022 (65/38). Wilma 2005 (95 kt, 60 nm), Irma 2017 (80 kt, 88 nm), Matthew 2016 (115 kt, 57 nm) and Milton 2024 (106 nm, crossed central FL) passed farther away but still affected the county. Historic direct hits: 1928 Okeechobee hurricane (125 kt, 3 nm) and 1949 (115 kt, 7 nm). NWS damage estimates for Palm Beach (search excerpts): Frances $500M, Jeanne $260M (roof damage mainly over Palm Beach County); Wilma caused moderate roof damage to many buildings with 3,600 workplaces reporting damage; Irma gusts 80-90 mph county-wide. NCEI Storm Events show hurricane-level county/zone entries only in 1996-2005 (10 events), none in 2006-2025 - the last 20 years were comparatively quiet, which may understate risk in owners' minds. ASCE 7-22 / FBC 8th ed. Risk Cat II Vult for West Palm Beach reported at ~160-170 mph (search summaries; confirm per parcel on the PBC wind-speed GIS).

roof_age_underwriting.text: Florida statute s. 627.7011 bars insurers from refusing or non-renewing a HOMEOWNER policy solely because a roof is under 15 years old and requires them to allow an inspection for roofs 15+ years - this protects residential only, not commercial property. For commercial buildings (search excerpts, low confidence): roof age and condition drive Florida commercial underwriting more than almost any other factor; older roofs draw non-renewals, higher deductibles, or roof surfacing settled at actual cash value (ACV) instead of replacement cost; ACV triggers are typically at 10, 15 or 20 years depending on carrier; private carriers typically tighten at 15-20 years through inspections and ACV shifts; Citizens publishes explicit roof-age rules (reported: 25-yr cap for shingle, 50-yr for tile/metal; ACV at 10 yrs for asphalt shingle - residential/shingle-focused, commercial low-slope rules not found). New policies on older roofs often require a roof inspection or wind-mitigation report; wind-mitigation features (roof deck attachment, roof-to-wall connections, secondary water resistance) earn premium credits under Florida's mandated wind-mitigation discount system. See data/national.json for ISO CP 10 36 (ACV roof surfacing endorsement). Sales implication: a documented biannual PaxSeal inspection record and condition reports directly address the inspection/ACV triggers carriers use.

wind_hail_deductible_norms.text: Florida commercial property named-storm/hurricane deductibles are percentage-based, typically 2%-10% of insured building value per storm (search excerpts from Florida agency guides); condo/HOA boards commonly choose between 5% and 10% named-storm deductibles. Example: a 5% deductible on a $2M building = $100,000 retained per hurricane. Florida statute requires $500, 2%, 5% and 10% hurricane-deductible options for residential policies (s. 627.701) - commercial deductibles are negotiated. 2026 market softening is bringing 'improved terms and lower deductibles than a year ago' for cat-exposed Florida accounts (broker commentary via search). Implication for the model: a single hurricane can put 2-5%+ of building value (the roof portion included) on the owner before insurance responds, so preventing roof-driven interior water losses has direct cash value.

roof_life_years.climate_note: Humid subtropical/tropical-monsoon coast (Köppen Am/Cfa boundary). Year-round high UV, summer surface temperatures reported above 160F on dark roofs, near-daily summer convective rain with wind-driven rain, biological growth, and salt air near the coast. NRI rates heat wave 'Relatively High', lightning 'Very High', strong wind 'Relatively High', and hurricane 'Very High'. Local contractors state a membrane rated 20-25 yrs in a moderate climate delivers 15-20 yrs in South Florida without diligent maintenance, and recommend twice-annual (spring and fall) inspections timed around hurricane season - which matches the PaxSeal biannual schedule. Ponding water at TPO welds/EPDM seams and clogged drains are cited as the most common preventable early failures.

code_triggers.text: Florida Building Code 8th Edition (2023), in force statewide; Palm Beach County is NOT in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (FBC-B Ch. 2: 'HIGH VELOCITY HURRICANE ZONE. This zone consists of Broward and Miami-Dade counties.' - read directly). HVHZ design wind speeds are fixed by FBC-B 1620.2 (Broward Risk Cat II 170 mph; Miami-Dade 175 mph); Palm Beach uses the ASCE 7-22 map (FBC-B 1609.3, parcel-specific via the county wind-speed GIS; ~160-170 mph Risk Cat II per search summaries) and is largely a wind-borne debris region. Secondary market Broward is HVHZ (FBC-B 1512-1525 roofing rules, product approvals, higher cost). (1) THE 25% RULE - FBC-Existing Building 706.1.1 (read directly): 'Not more than 25 percent of the total roof area or roof section of any existing building or structure shall be repaired, replaced or recovered in any 12-month period unless the roof covering on the entire existing roof system or roof section is replaced or recovered to conform to the requirements of this code.' EXCEPTION (added by SB 4-D, 2022; F.S. 553.844(5)): if the existing roofing system or section was built, repaired or replaced in compliance with the 2007 FBC or later, and 25% or more is being repaired/replaced/recovered, only the repaired portion must meet current code; local governments may not amend this exception. The 2007 FBC took effect 1 Mar 2009 (per search excerpts), so roofs installed before ~2009 still face the all-or-nothing rule: a storm that damages >25% of an old roof section forces full replacement of that section. SALES POINT: a pre-2009 roof is a latent full-replacement liability; a documented, well-maintained post-2009 roof can be repaired in place after a storm. (2) RECOVER VS REPLACE - FBC-EB 706.3: tear-off to deck is required when the existing roof is water-soaked or deteriorated, has two or more coverings, has blisters not cut/secured, or cannot meet FBC 1504.1 securement for a new system attached through it; coatings over SPF and separate structural standing-seam systems are allowed without tear-off. Wet insulation (a typical outcome of deferred leak repair) therefore eliminates the cheaper recover/restoration option. (3) SECONDARY WATER BARRIER & DECK ATTACHMENT - FBC-EB 706.7/706.7.2 require re-nailing of wood decks and a secondary water barrier on reroof of WOOD-deck structures; slopes < 2:12 with a continuous roof system are deemed to comply, and structures originally permitted under the FBC are exempt - so most steel-deck low-slope warehouses/offices are largely unaffected. (4) ROOF-TO-WALL CONNECTIONS - FBC-EB 706.8: on reroof of a wood-deck building in the wind-borne debris region with insured (or just) value >= $300,000, roof-to-wall connections must be improved per 706.8.1, capped at 15% of reroofing cost; exempt if permitted under the FBC. (5) ROOF DIAPHRAGM - FBC-EB 707.3.2: where the structural deck is removed from >30% of the diaphragm and Vult > 115 mph (true for all of Palm Beach County), roof diaphragm, diaphragm-to-framing and roof-to-wall connections must be evaluated and strengthened if below 75% of current wind loads (exempt for buildings permitted under the FBC). Deck corrosion found late (after years of leaks) can trigger this. (6) STRUCTURAL - FBC-EB 707.2: added dead load >5% triggers gravity check, except a second roof layer <= 3 psf over a single existing layer. (7) ENERGY - FBC-EB 708.1: alterations must comply with the FBC-Energy Conservation; the specific reroof insulation requirement (IECC C503-style) and R-value for climate zone 1/2 were NOT verified. (8) Reroofing need not meet the 2% minimum slope if positive drainage exists (FBC-EB 706.1; HVHZ has separate rules). Rusted flashing/edge metal/drain outlets may not be reinstalled (706.5).
